gender.note: No default at the hub: it always refuses `auto` and an absent gender (400). `auto` is the CALLER's configured default (its per-agent classifier) and must be resolved client-side into `female` or `male` before the descriptor is sent, because the hub has no agent context to classify.

tone.note: An unknown token is a NEWER CLIENT than this hub, so it degrades to the nearest tone with a note rather than a 400.

pace.note: 1.0 is normal speech; a value outside the accepted range is a 400, an accepted value outside a provider's own range is clamped with a note.

language.note: `auto` means the caller sends no language and the vendor auto-detects.

accent.note: Honoured only where a provider takes instructions text; a provider with no instructions field ignores it with a note.

instructions.note: The default is the pre-#1835 native-dialect guidance. It lives in the CALLER's config, beside its consumer, so the caller resolves the default before sending and the hub adds nothing when the field is absent.

request_providers.note: `radient` is not a provider a request may name: it is what omitting `provider` gets you (the hub's own cascade, which owns leg choice), so the radient capability row is a promise about the composite and the response headers name the leg that actually served.

gender.detail: the hub's own cascade always serves a voice from the logical pool

tone.detail: honoured as a pool row on ElevenLabs, emulated as an instructions sentence on OpenAI; the hub owns leg choice, so the map states the weaker guarantee

expressiveness.detail: honoured as voice_settings.stability on ElevenLabs, emulated on OpenAI

pace.detail: clamped per leg: 0.7-1.2 on ElevenLabs, 0.25-4 on OpenAI

language.detail: ElevenLabs' default model (eleven_multilingual_v2) drops language_code; only eleven_flash_v2_5 enforces it

accent.detail: only reachable through OpenAI instructions emulation, which the primary leg does not take

instructions.detail: ElevenLabs has no instructions field and this integration never folds instructions into the synthesized text

tone.detail: voice pool row; the v1 tone rows share the two verified voices, so variety within a gender comes from voice_settings.stability

expressiveness.detail: voice_settings.stability: high 0.35, medium 0.5, low 0.7 (today's constant is 0.5, so medium is unchanged)

language.detail: only on the models listed here, via language_code; eleven_multilingual_v2 drops it with a note

accent.detail: no field, and the integration never folds a hint into the text

instructions.detail: no field; never folded into the text

gender.detail: voice from the pool; the vendor does not document voice gender, so the pool's labels are our judgement

tone.detail: pool voice plus a fixed tone sentence appended to instructions

language.detail: instructions sentence; gpt-4o-mini-tts takes no language parameter

instructions.detail: the instructions field, capped at 8000 characters

tone_phrase.warm: Speak in a warm, friendly tone.
tone_phrase.neutral: Speak in a neutral, even tone.
tone_phrase.bright: Speak in a bright, upbeat tone.
tone_phrase.calm: Speak in a calm, unhurried tone.
tone_phrase.authoritative: Speak in an authoritative, confident tone.

language_phrase.openai: Speak the text in the language it is written in, and pronounce foreign words as a native speaker of that language would.

accent_phrase.openai: Adapt the pronunciation for the %s accent.

nearest.voice_row: exact (gender, tone) row -> same gender with warm -> same gender's first row -> the female warm row

provenance.elevenlabs_voice_ids: verified by a 200 synthesis with the production key; not name-confirmable against GET /v1/voices for this account (docs/SPEECH.md, Voices)
provenance.tone_phrases: authored here, not vendor-published; a MINOR bump may revise them
